Exposure                    Replacement.
Exposure                    Replacement.

[VISUAL DESCRIPTION]
This is an infographic slide. The heading or title concept presented is "Exposure ≠ Replacement," indicated by the not-equal symbol between the two words at the top of the image. The visual contains two primary percentage figures: **59%** on the left side labeled "HIGH EXPOSURE TO AI," and **41%** on the right side, which by context represents the portion of the workforce that does not have high exposure to AI. A horizontal bar at the bottom of the image is divided proportionally, with approximately 59% shown in blue and 41% shown in grey, visually reinforcing the split. The bar is labeled **"QUÉBEC WORKFORCE (2.7 MILLION PEOPLE)"**, indicating the total population being referenced is 2.7 million individuals. There are no traditional axis labels, column headers, or scatter plot elements, as this is a stylized infographic rather than a chart. The central visual motif features a human head silhouette split between a detailed biological brain on the left (colored, representing exposure) and a digital/circuit-style brain on the right (faded, representing lesser exposure or non-replacement). The key insight is that **59% of Québec's workforce of 2.7 million people has high exposure to AI**, but the title explicitly emphasizes that exposure does **not** equal replacement — distinguishing between jobs being transformed versus eliminated. No source or citation is visibly credited in the image.

Change is situational. Transition is psychological.
Change is situational. Transition is psychological.

[VISUAL DESCRIPTION]
This is an infographic/diagram slide depicting William Bridges' Transition Model. The heading reads "Change is situational. Transition is psychological." There are no numerical data points, percentages, axis labels, or column headers present in this visual, as it is a conceptual process diagram rather than a data-driven chart. The diagram consists of three sequential arrow shapes moving from left to right, each representing a distinct phase of psychological transition. The first arrow is styled in dark teal/blue and is labeled "ENDING" with the subtitle "Letting go of the old," accompanied by a circular icon below depicting a broken chain link. The second arrow is styled in dark gray/purple and is labeled "NEUTRAL ZONE" with the subtitle "The time in-between," accompanied by a circular icon below depicting a winding or serpentine path. The third arrow is styled in orange/amber and is labeled "NEW BEGINNING" with the subtitle "Starting fresh," accompanied by a circular icon below depicting a flowering plant or sprout in an orange-bordered circle. The neutral zone arrow also features a circular swirling graphic overlaid on it, suggesting ambiguity or cyclical uncertainty during that phase. The key insight is that external change (situational) and internal psychological transition are distinct processes, and that humans must psychologically move through an ending, navigate an uncertain in-between period, and ultimately arrive at a new beginning. No source attribution is visible in the image.

The visual depicts a **ladder or scaffold structure** rendered in a metallic silver/chrome 3D style, rising diagonally from the lower left to the upper right against a soft blue sky background with sparkle/glitter particle effects. The ladder has three rungs, each represented by a **cylindrical metallic bar**, and each rung is labeled with a different intelligence quotient acronym and a positional descriptor: the bottom rung is labeled **"IQ — Base"**, the middle rung is labeled **"EQ — Middle"**, and the top rung — which extends upward into clouds — is labeled **"AQ — Peak"**. The key insight or takeaway of this infographic is that IQ (Intelligence Quotient) forms the foundational base of human capability, EQ (Emotional Quotient) represents a middle layer of advancement, and AQ (Adaptability Quotient) is positioned as the ultimate, highest-level differentiator — the "peak" or game-changer — particularly relevant in modern career, employment, or AI-driven contexts. No source attribution is visible anywhere in the image.

The three rungs of the ladder are labeled from bottom to top as follows: the lowest rung reads "IQ" with the subtext "Base," the middle rung reads "EQ" with the subtext "Middle," and the uppermost rung reads "AQ" with the subtext "Peak," with this top rung dissolving into clouds and sparkling light, suggesting it represents the highest or most aspirational level. Calm the Fight-or-Flight.
Calm the Fight-or-Flight.

[VISUAL DESCRIPTION]
This image is an animated infographic or interactive breathing exercise visual, not a careers, employment, or AI document. The heading reads "Calm the Fight-or-Flight." in bold white text in the upper left corner. The visual consists of two concentric circles — an inner solid white glowing circle and an outer ring made of dotted/dashed points — with a circular arc (progress indicator) and three small white dot markers positioned at approximately the left middle (9 o'clock), right middle (3 o'clock), and bottom center (6 o'clock) positions on the outer circle. The three data points or instructional labels visible are: "INHALE 4" on the left side, "HOLD 7" at the top center, and "EXHALE 8" on the right side. These numbers represent seconds for each breathing phase in the 4-7-8 breathing technique. There are no axis labels, column headers, or source citations visible. There is a curved white arc line that appears to be animating around the circle to guide the user through the breathing phases. The key insight is that this is a guided breathing exercise visualization using the 4-7-8 breathing method — inhale for 4 seconds, hold for 7 seconds, exhale for 8 seconds — designed to activate the parasympathetic nervous system and reduce acute stress or anxiety responses (fight-or-flight). No source attribution is visible in the image.

There are no axis labels, column headers, chart axes, or tabular data present in this image. There is no visible source citation. The visual metaphor combines the depleted battery at 20% with the chaotic overflow of documents to suggest that excessive or poor-quality work/information overload is a significant drain on energy, focus, and productive output in a professional or AI-assisted work context.

The key takeaway is that AI readiness is framed as a multi-dimensional human capability model encompassing five interconnected competencies — agility, mindset, literacy, experimentation, and feedback — suggesting that organizational or individual preparedness for AI requires development across all five of these distinct but complementary areas.
